speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To understand the onset and progression of these symptoms, can you tell me how long these issues have been developing?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The combination of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, and speech slurring raises concern for a spinal cord or brainstem pathology. Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness specifically in your legs or arms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of rigidity, mild hand tremor, and orthostatic hypotension alongside your gait issues and urinary incontinence is highly suggestive of a parkinsonian syndrome or a specific neurodegenerative condition like Multiple System Atrophy (MSA). Can you describe the nature of your tremor, and do you experience any falls or dizziness when standing up?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with focus on brainstem and cerebellum.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI confirms neurodegenerative changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, which aligns with your symptoms of parkinsonism, ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction. Given the prominent cerebellar and autonomic involvement, do you or your family notice any difficulty with swallowing (dysphagia) or nasal regurgitation?

REQUEST TEST: Autonomic_Functions_Panel
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brainstem_Coronal

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Autonomic_Testing: Marked orthostatic hypotension without compensatory tachycardia, indicating autonomic dysfunction. MRI_Brain_and_Spinal_Cord: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C). The combination of prominent cerebellar atrophy, severe autonomic dysfunction (orthostatic hypotension without tachycardia), and parkinsonian features confirms this diagnosis.
